title: The Courage to Criticize Imperialism
author: Thomas Sankara
context: Conducted in January 1987 by TASS special envoy Boris Chabaev following the 1986 Reykjavik summit between Mikhail Gorbachev and Ronald Reagan, this interview presents Captain Thomas Sankara’s vision of Pan-African anti-imperialism, global disarmament, and national sovereignty for Burkina Faso and the Global South.
relatesToToday: Offers a vital framework for understanding how modern developing nations confront imperialist hegemony, covert foreign destabilization, and the ongoing struggle for genuine multipolar sovereignty and self-determined economic development.
keyTakeaways: World peace and disarmament are not the exclusive preserve of superpowers; imperialist warfare and ecological crises directly impact the developing world.
African liberation demands collective courage in continental forums like the OAU to expose neocolonial exploitation, foreign military bases, and armed proxy destabilization.
Raising popular anti-imperialist consciousness among workers and peasants is the prerequisite for overcoming underdevelopment and achieving national self-reliance.
